name: pio_usb_hub_recovery
description: Everything the design doc's power-and-recovery gate names that is not a route test: every downstream hub port replugged, the hub cable itself unplugged and replugged at the TYPE-C EXP socket, U2/PC2 disconnected and reconnected, a key held through a detach, rapid mixed input straight afterward, and RGB switched on and off while watching for a brownout. If RGB operation causes a reset or an enumeration loss, that is a failed power gate by itself, independent of every other check here - a bigger PTC does not override the PC port's or the hub module's own current limit.
requires: U1 flashed with the pio-pio-usb-release image, the hub, keyboard and mouse already enumerated (run pio_usb_hub_enumeration.json first)
U2 on SPI1, wired GP10<->GP10, GP9<->GP9, U1 GP11->U2 GP8, U2 GP11->U1 GP8, common GND, and PC2 attached to U2
A keyboard with RGB lighting that can be switched on and off from its own controls, or the current wired keyboard if it has no RGB - state which on the report either way
The Keychron 2.4GHz receiver, if available, on its own downstream port
A CDC session to U1 to run GET_DIAGNOSTICS before and after each replug (operator-supplied port; not hard-coded here)
on_this_rig: endpoint_reconnect_clean and backend_error_counters_stable are both decided from GET_DIAGNOSTICS alone, with a baseline taken before each replug and a reading taken after the port is ready again. detach_releases_observed needs a computer watching what a held key does when its source is unplugged, and this rig has no logger at PC1 or PC2, so it stays unmeasured here regardless of what actually happened - a human at each computer is what decides it. The RGB power gate is watched entirely by a human: nothing on U1's own diagnostics distinguishes a brownout reset from a normal boot, so a reset during this step is read from the device physically re-enumerating and from GET_DIAGNOSTICS's own uptime-since-boot resetting to near zero, not inferred from a counter. If U2 is not attached for part of this run, link_crc_errors and link_frames_sent climb together at the same rate - a live measurement on this bench read 7428/7428 with zero echoed frames - so this scenario names no check that reads those two counters as evidence of link quality; a scenario that did would read an absent U2 as a catastrophically broken one instead of as what it is.

steps.note: phase-baseline reading, taken with the hub, keyboard, mouse and U2 all already attached and settled
unplug whichever peripheral is on this port
everything behind the hub has to re-enumerate from nothing
phase-measure reading for endpoint_reconnect_clean and backend_error_counters_stable, scoped to the replugs above
leave it held, then detach this peripheral - the release is only visible at the computer it was routed to
unplug the keyboard while key_a is still held
unmeasurable on this rig; recorded manually
rapid alternating keyboard and mouse input immediately after the reattach above, to catch a backend that reconnected but did not rearm cleanly
unplug U2 from PC2 while PC1 keeps receiving input
switch the keyboard's own RGB lighting on, watching U1 and the hub for any reset or re-enumeration

checks.both_devices_ready: after every replug in this run, the keyboard slot and the mouse slot both reached ready again
checks.endpoint_reconnect_clean: the replugged port(s) reached ready again with no duplicate mount recorded for the reconnect
checks.backend_error_counters_stable: no backend error counter grew across the whole sequence of replugs
checks.detach_releases_observed: no key or button remained held at PC1 or PC2 after any detach in this run

failure_criteria.both_devices_ready: any replug in the sequence leaves a slot attached but never ready, or leaves diagnostics reporting nothing attached at all, more than 5 seconds after the physical replug
failure_criteria.endpoint_reconnect_clean: duplicate_mounts is higher after the replug sequence than before it, or a port that was replugged never returns to ready
failure_criteria.backend_error_counters_stable: any of event_overflows, detach_overflows, stale_events_discarded, arm_failures, arm_escalations, device_overflows, interface_overflows or callback_overflows is higher after the sequence than the baseline taken before it started
failure_criteria.detach_releases_observed: a key or button pressed before a detach is still reported as held at the computer it was routed to, at any point after the detach

manual_observations.item: hub cable replug at the TYPE-C EXP socket
manual_observations.expected: unplugging and replugging the cable that carries the whole hub causes every downstream device to re-enumerate within a few seconds of the replug, with no key left held at either computer from before the cable was pulled
manual_observations.fail_if: a downstream device fails to re-enumerate after the hub cable is restored, or a key held before the cable was pulled is still reported held at either computer afterward

manual_observations.item: PC2 disconnect while PC1 remains active
manual_observations.expected: unplugging U2 from PC2 leaves PC1 receiving keyboard and mouse input without interruption; reconnecting PC2 brings U2 back without needing U1 to be power-cycled
manual_observations.fail_if: PC1 loses input while U2/PC2 is disconnected, or U2 does not resume answering once PC2 is reconnected

manual_observations.item: detach while a key is held
manual_observations.expected: unplugging the keyboard mid-press releases the held key at the computer it was routed to, within roughly the same order of magnitude as U2's own 100 ms link-loss release budget - this rig cannot time it, but a human watching the far computer can see whether it happens at all
manual_observations.fail_if: the key stays reported as held at the far computer any length of time after the physical unplug

manual_observations.expected: unplugging and replugging the receiver re-establishes both its keyboard-role and mouse-role ports, including the side button on interface 2, without needing U1 to be restarted
manual_observations.fail_if: the receiver comes back missing the keyboard role, missing the side button's report, or claiming a role it did not have before the replug

manual_observations.item: RGB power gate - keyboard RGB lighting switched on and off
manual_observations.expected: no reset, brownout or loss of enumeration on U1, the hub, or any attached peripheral while RGB is on, at any brightness the keyboard's own controls reach
manual_observations.fail_if: U1, the hub, or a peripheral resets, browns out or drops off the bus while RGB is enabled - this is a failed power gate on its own, independent of every other check in this scenario, and the first response is to reduce peripheral power or move to a powered-hub revision, not to enlarge the PTC
